newsitem.title: USA: NYSE approves new triggers for circuit-breakers.
newsitem.headline: NYSE approves new triggers for circuit-breakers.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said its board of directors has approved a proposal to increase the trigger points for market-wide circuit-breakers.

The action, the result of a joint effort by the NYSE and the Securities and Exchange Commission calls for a half-hour trading halt across all U.S. equities and futures markets if the Dow Jones Industrial Average falls 350 points from the previous day's close; and a one-hour halt at minus 550 points.
The current levels are 250 and 400 points, respectively.

The exchange said that, in recent months, it has been discussing with its constituents the appropriate level of the circuit-breakers and the Securities and Exchange Commission has urged U.S. equities markets to evaluate the trigger points in view of the stock market's rally since the curbs were established in 1988.
The 50-point trigger on program trading curbs is believed to be unchanged. The NYSE was not available for comment.

"The new proposal reflects a consensus among our constituents to balance the need to give investors a period of market calm following a sharp, quick market downturn, and our commitment to maintain public access to and participation in the marketplace, said NYSE chief executive Richard Grasso.

The NYSE said it will continue to periodically re-evaluate the trigger points of all circuit-breakers to assess whether changes are warranted. The 250 and 400 point circuit-breakers were enacted in October 1988 and the time frames of the halts were reduced to 30 minutes and one hour, respectively, in July.
